Use "rwx docs [command] --help" for more information about a command.

# CLI triggers

A CLI trigger configures runs started from the CLI with `rwx run` by adding an `on.cli` block to your run definition. See [Event Triggers](/docs/event-triggers) for options shared across all trigger types, and [Event Fields](/docs/cli-triggers#event-fields) for the `event` fields available on CLI events.

## Defining a CLI trigger

```yaml
on:
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}

```

When you run `rwx run .rwx/ci.yml`, RWX will use the `cli` trigger configuration.

## Testing workflows locally

You can start run definitions from the CLI without committing or pushing. `rwx run` picks up your local edits and applies them to the `git/clone` task, so you can iterate faster without having to push changes to a git remote.

Inside a git repository, `rwx run` finds the most recent commit in your branch's history that's already on your remote — the closest ancestor your local `HEAD` shares with `origin`, even if your branch itself has never been pushed — and uses that as the base for the run. `event.git.sha` resolves to that commit. The CLI then sends a patch on top covering everything from there to your working tree: local commits you haven't pushed, uncommitted edits, and new untracked files. With that patch applied, the `git/clone` task will match your local state.

Files ignored by your `.gitignore` are not included.

## Event fields

The following fields are available on CLI events. They're derived from your local git state at the moment you run `rwx run`.

| attribute        | description                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| event.git.sha    | The most recent commit in your branch's history that's already on your remote — the closest ancestor your local HEAD shares with origin. Used as the base commit for the locally-sent patch. |
| event.git.ref    | The full git ref derived from your local branch. Example: refs/heads/main. Not set when in a detached HEAD state.                                                                            |
| event.git.branch | The current branch name (event.git.ref with refs/heads/ stripped). Empty when in a detached HEAD state.                                                                                      |

If RWX can't determine your local git state — for example, git isn't installed, you aren't inside a git repository, no remote is configured, or your branch shares no commits with the remote — `event.git.*` lookups fail with a descriptive error message naming the cause.

## Best practices

### Hard-coding init parameters

A common pattern is to hard-code certain `init` parameters in your CLI trigger to simplify local testing. For example:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        environment: production
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      environment: development

```

In this example, runs triggered from the CLI will always use the `development` environment, while runs triggered from GitHub pushes will use `production`. This removes the need to pass `--init environment=development` every time you run from the CLI.

### Targeting specific tasks

# RWX CLI in this repo

CI definitions live in `.rwx/` (`tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml`, `validate-assets.yml`, `trunk-impacted-targets.yml`). Each has an `on.cli` trigger, so it can be started locally.

## Auth: two injected tokens, one per RWX workspace

Two env vars are injected into the environment. Each token is scoped to one RWX workspace (organization):

| Env var | Workspace |
| --- | --- |
| `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_MARCHILI` | marchili |
| `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO` | elviskahoro (note the `RWC_` prefix, not `RWX_`) |

The workspace names are inferred from the variable names. Confirm which one owns this repo's runs (try `rwx runs list` with each) before relying on it.

The CLI reads only `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (or `--access-token`), so export the one you want under that name. Do this per command and never print the token:

```bash
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="$RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_MARCHILI"      # marchili workspace
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="$RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO"   # elviskahoro workspace
# or, one-off:
rwx runs list --access-token "$RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO"
```

A run, task, or log ID only resolves under the workspace that owns it. If a lookup returns not-found or unauthorized, switch tokens.

## Running a pipeline with your current git changes

`rwx run` sends a git patch with the run, so no commit or push is needed:

- Base: the closest ancestor of local `HEAD` that is already on `origin`. `event.git.sha` resolves to it.
- Patch on top: unpushed local commits, staged changes, unstaged changes, and untracked files.
- Excluded: anything in `.gitignore`. Git LFS changes error out; commit and push those first.
- `RWX_DISABLE_GIT_PATCH=1` turns patching off.

```bash
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --wait --fail-fast          # run CI on the working tree, wait for result
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --target <task-key> --wait  # only one task (and its dependencies)
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --title "wip: my change" --json
```

The `git/clone` task takes `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}`, and the `cli` trigger sets `commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}`. That wiring is what makes the patch apply, so keep it when editing `.rwx/*.yml`. Edits to the `.rwx` files themselves are also picked up locally.

## Logs and results

```bash
rwx runs list
rwx results <run-id>                          # status and failures for a run
rwx logs <task-id>                            # download logs for a task
rwx logs <run-id> --task <task-key> --output /tmp/logs
```

`rwx run` prints the run URL and ID. Use `--json` for parsing.

## Docs

`rwx docs search "<query>"` and `rwx docs pull /docs/cli-triggers` (also `/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run`).
